people.name: Ali Ahmad
people.short_bio: A revenue expert in the Revenue Department who understands home wiring and solar installation and works out loads, watts, solar output and running costs himself.
bio: Ali Ahmad lives in Okara, Pakistan. He holds an MA in Sociology and has worked as a revenue expert in the Revenue Department since 2021.

He understands how home wiring and solar systems are put together and works out costs, watts, solar output, loads and running costs himself. He is not a licensed electrician or engineer, which is why the formulas are documented on the methodology page and checked by a separate technical review.

He built Wattlyst because amps, watts, units, bill slabs and taxes are hard to understand, and knowing them saves electricity: a lower bill for the home and less waste for the country. The tools turn those numbers into a clear answer anyone can use.
people.bio_source: Facts given by Ali Ahmad in the project thread, 21 October 2026 (audit 2026-10-21 Phase 8, WL-215). Change only with the owner's own words.

tou.fixed_basis: higher of 50% sanctioned load or MDI

peak_hours.applies_to: ex-WAPDA DISCOs (LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO, GEPCO, FESCO, PESCO, HESCO, SEPCO, QESCO, TESCO), consumers on a Time-of-Use meter (5 kW or more sanctioned load); every other hour is off-peak

income_tax_235.applies_to: domestic consumers not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List (ATL); monthly bill of Rs 25,000 or more

net_billing.buyback_basis: Regulation 14(1)(b): units a prosumer exports are billed at the national average energy purchase price (NAEPP). Regulation 14(3): NEPRA may revise the rate by notification.
net_billing.existing_prosumers: Agreements signed before 9 Feb 2026 stay on the rate and mechanism of the repealed 2015 net-metering regulations until they expire (SRO 547(I)/2026, 2 Apr 2026, substitutes regulation 21(2), deemed effective 9 Feb 2026; the first version had set them at the national average power purchase price). A material modification that changes the maximum output (e.g. adding panels) ends those terms early. Renewals move to net billing (regulation 21(3)).

methods.B1: In conduit in a brick or plastered (masonry) wall, most Pakistani house wiring; a conduit buried in thermal insulation is method A1 and is rated lower
methods.C: Clipped direct to a wall or surface

B.use: lighting, sockets and resistive loads (heaters, irons, geysers)

C.use: air conditioners, fridges, motors, water pumps and mixed socket circuits

D.use: transformers, welding machines and large motors with heavy inrush

derating._status: default_ambient_c is a conservative Pakistani summer design value pending PEC engineer review; ratings at 30 C are kept in the table above

methods.surface: Clipped on a roof, frame or tray surface
methods.free_air: In free air, spaced from surfaces
methods.touching: Two cables touching on a surface (positive and negative together)
